variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create ONE new production concept sheet for a bolder pirate refit of the Liberty heavy fighter from Freelancer (2003), code L03. The priority is an interesting three-dimensional hull silhouette, with substantial HEIGHT, authentic Liberty Art Deco construction and the unchanged original cockpit. A practical pirate combat craft repaired with substitute sections.

REFERENCE ROLES, in supplied order:
1: The authoritative IMMUTABLE target cockpit, enlarged from the actual li_pir_elite model. Copy this capsule, its shell, pane outlines, narrow frames and mounting exactly in every view.
2: The actual target li_pir_elite in deployed flight: body scale, three collar flanges, inclined fan wings, two vertically stacked engines.
3: Same-scale neutral geometry comparison. Columns left to right: li_pir_elite, li_elite, or_elite, li_elite2. Borrow the THIRD column's sculpted shoulders and tiered vertical stern; borrow the FOURTH column's swept rising dorsal profile. These donors do NOT replace the target cockpit or mechanical layout.
4: The same four ships textured. Observe their structural Art Deco vocabulary and the target's muted pirate materials.
5: Historical Mercenary Elite Fighter art: use only the streamlined stepped body and fan rhythms. Its short high arch cockpit is DIFFERENT and MUST NOT be used.

NEW SHAPE — make a deliberate redesign, not an embellished rectangular slab:
Keep the original low rounded forward cockpit and its three transverse collar flanges. Immediately behind the collar, the hull shoulders rise and widen through angular nested trapezoids. Give each flank a deep substantial diagonal recessed cove with solid sloping walls, flowing into a broad enclosed fan-root socket. The lower hull has a purposeful deep faceted belly and an upward rear cut, with real volume beneath the shoulders.
Behind the central cargo hatch, build a HIGH, swept-back aft haunch: a thick integrated engine housing rising in two offset sloping terraces, with a clipped angular crest and one broad inset mechanical field. It should grow out of the hull and taper in plan, not be a thin airplane fin attached to a flat roof. The rear profile has a clear rise, step and return; avoid a long level rectangle. A compact solid aft equipment ledge integrates with this stepped stern. Give the shoulders, belly and stern distinct but connected contours and clear negative spaces at their transitions.
Maintain the stock ship's width and length approximately (about 14 by 15 source units); allow height around 7.5, above the target's 6 but below the towering donor fins near 9.5. These numbers describe proportions, do not print dimensions. Do not squash or vertically sink the body, do not lengthen it into a thin plank. The silhouette must still feel like a maneuverable heavy fighter.

COCKPIT LOCK:
Visually transplant image 1's elongated rounded glazed capsule, at its original physical size, out in front of the collar. Preserve the broad curved side windows, long central roof pane, small rear side panes, rounded glazed nose and lower glazing. There is NO solid pointed nose ahead of this capsule. It is not a little canopy perched atop a new fuselage. Keep it outside and forward of the shoulders, with the same short neck, original shell and window layout. Do not copy donor glazing, add forehead armor, narrow the glass into slits or invent extra frames. Body changes begin behind the unchanged collar and cabin.

WINGS AND MECHANISMS:
Each side has THREE connected, overlapping SOLID FAN LEAVES in deployed flight, inclined downward at the root like image 2. Preserve that fan topology; make the leaves purposeful angular sectors with broad inset fields, clipped pointed tips and a clear stepped outer silhouette. Their inclined chained joints fold the leaves inward/back to nest for docking. Roots sit in functional solid recessed sockets; no external skeletons or rods. Do not adopt or_elite's sliding wing system.
The center-top cargo hatch remains TWO LONGITUDINAL closed doors side by side. Their seam follows the ship's FRONT-TO-BACK centerline, NOT a transverse line dividing front and rear panels. Each hinges along its outer long edge and opens outward/up; keep the entire door zone and sweep clear of fixed shoulders and dorsal structure. The raised aft haunch starts BEHIND the hatch.
Exactly TWO aft-facing exhausts stacked VERTICALLY, one above the other on the centerline, upper larger, lower smaller. No side-by-side engine pods and no third exhaust. In strict top view, the lower engine is occluded beneath the upper, not moved sideways for visibility.

STYLE AND PIRATE CHARACTER:
Liberty Art Deco expressed as stepped massing, swept parallel planes, fan geometry and nested trapezoidal recesses. Broad structural transitions and medium-sized mechanical details matter more than texture. Design visible replacement hull modules, reinforced inset hinge seats, a few irregular repair joints and mismatched armor sections which belong to the load-bearing body. Keep paired primary volumes balanced; small maintenance asymmetry is welcome.
Weathered dark oxide red/brown, soot-dark recessed fields, several dull pale steel replacement areas, original blue-grey glazing. Restrained wear and medium-rich readable detail. Neither bare minimalist boxes nor a carpet of micro-greebles. No skulls, demons, horns, spikes, flags, gold filigree, exposed tubes, wire bundles, scaffolding or tiny modeled rivets.

SHEET:
Landscape on pale warm-grey paper. ONE consistent design in THREE views: large front-side three-quarter perspective occupying the upper portion, nose LEFT; below, a substantial clean SIDE PROFILE with the FULL raised stern and belly clearly visible, and a strict TOP VIEW with deployed fan wings. Use consistent proportions and panel locations across views. All ships fully within generous margins. Polished painted production concept, crisp purposeful edges, studio light with readable recess shadows, no scenery and no external weapons obscuring form. Only text: "LI PIR ELITE — L03", "SIDE", "TOP".

scope: Concept-art prototype only. Current li_pir_elite cabin and mechanics remain authoritative. Not approved for modeling.
user_direction: Более дерзкий пиратский дизайн; не занижать высоту; интересная форма на основе li_elite, or_elite, li_elite2.
